title: Product Gaussian Hessian integral bound
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set, let $c\in\mathbb R^I$, and let $v$ be a nonzero nonnegative real number. Let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$. For any $i,j\in I$, under the product of Gaussian measures with means $c_k$ and common variance $v$, \[\left|\int_{\mathbb R^I}\left(\frac{(z_i-c_i)(z_j-c_j)}{v^2}-\frac{\delta_{ij}}{v}\right)f(z)\,d\mu(z)\right|\le\frac2v,\] where $\delta_{ij}=1$ when $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $v$ is a nonzero nonnegative real number
replaced: Let $I$ be a finite set, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v>0$, and $\mu_{c,v}=\bigotimes_{i\in I}N(c_i,v)$. For $i,j\in I$, put $H_{ij}(z)=(z_i-c_i)(z_j-c_j)/v^2-\delta_{ij}/v$, where $\delta_{ij}$ is one if $i=j$ and zero otherwise. For any $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ with $|f|\le1$ and $i,j\in I$, $|\int H_{ij}f\,d\mu_{c,v}|\le2/v$, assigning zero to a nonintegrable integral.
